text:
objective: To conduct a decadal analysis and simulation of land use and land cover (LULC) changes in Taiwan from 1990 to 2020 and project future LULC for 2030 and 2050 under multiple scenarios, incorporating demographic trends such as negative population growth, using machine learning and Markov chain models.
country: Taiwan
land_use_classes: barren; uncultivated; shallow water; deep water; built-up; forest; cultivated
baseline_years: 1990; 2000; 2010; 2020
target_future_years: 2030; 2050
scenarios: 2-variables (elevation, distance to roads); 3-variables (elevation, distance to roads, distance to rivers); 5-variables (aspect, elevation, hillshade, distance to rivers, slope); 6-variables (aspect, elevation, hillshade, distance to rivers, distance to roads, slope)
analysis_methods: Supervised classification using maximum likelihood classifier; Support Vector Machine (SVM) for LULC classification; Markov-chain method for LULC simulation; accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, kappa coefficient, producer’s and user’s accuracy, and RMSE
simulation_method_advantages: The SVM-Markov chain hybrid approach leverages precise LULC classification capabilities of SVM and probabilistic transition modeling of Markov chains, improving simulation accuracy in complex urban landscapes; this integrated method is applied at a national scale for the first time in Taiwan and accounts for multiple environmental predictors under varying scenarios.
predictors: aspect; elevation; hillshade; distance to river; distance to road; slope
population_selected: Yes
data_sources: Landsat 5, 7, and 8 Surface Reflectance Tier 1 satellite images (1990–2020); Shuttle Radar Topographic Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Model (30 m) for aspect, elevation, hillshade, slope, and distance to rivers; OpenStreetMap and Google Earth for road data; Google Earth Engine for image preprocessing and ROI extraction
tools_software_used: Google Earth Engine; GIS software (implied but not explicitly named); SVM and Markov-chain modeling frameworks (specific software not named)
validation_performed: Yes
validation_methods: Confusion matrix; overall accuracy; kappa coefficient; producer’s accuracy; user’s accuracy; RMSE; comparison of simulated 2020 LULC with actual 2020 classified LULC
validation_data_sources: Ground control points (GCPs)—655 for classification validation and 300 for 2020 prediction validation; actual Landsat-derived 2020 LULC map
key_findings: Built-up area increased by ~140% from 1990 to 2020 (from 1,027.74 km² to 2,476.30 km²); under the 6-variable scenario, built-up area is projected to increase by 223% from 1990 levels by 2050; barren land decreased by ~49% from 1990 to 2020 and is projected to decline further; despite negative population growth, impervious surface area continues to expand; forest and cultivated areas slightly increased due to conservation efforts; the 3-variable scenario yielded the most reliable simulation results with fewer predictors.
implications: Continued urban expansion despite declining population suggests inefficient land use and potential overdevelopment; findings highlight the need for infill development, revitalization of existing urban areas, and stronger conservation policies; results can inform national land-use planning, infrastructure investment, and decarbonization strategies in Taiwan and similar regions.
limitations: Reliance on static transition probabilities in the Markov model assumes stationarity, ignoring potential non-linear or policy-driven shifts; exclusion of socio-economic variables beyond population trends (e.g., GDP, land policies); limited accuracy of moderate-resolution Landsat imagery in dense urban areas; assumption of spatial independence between cells overlooks neighborhood effects.
future_directions: Incorporate dynamic transition probabilities and socio-economic drivers (e.g., housing demand, policy scenarios); integrate object-based classification to improve urban LULC accuracy; extend simulations to include carbon emission modeling; apply the framework to other mid-sized, rapidly urbanizing island nations.
scalability: The methodology is scalable to other regions with similar topographic complexity and urbanization dynamics, especially mid-sized countries undergoing demographic transitions; however, local calibration of predictors and validation data would be required.
novelty: First national-scale LULC simulation study for Taiwan spanning 1990–2050; integration of SVM classification with Markov-chain simulation at country level; explicit consideration of negative population growth in LULC forecasting; multi-scenario testing with systematic variable inclusion to assess predictor influence.
